Prospective sample size and statistical power calculation for clinical data audits

Source: R/audit-power.R
catmech_audit_power.Rd

Computes the statistical power and sample size required to achieve a target confidence interval precision ratio (\(\rho \le \rho_{target}\)) in a two-phase clinical audit. Can evaluate power prospectively from prior clinical error parameters or empirically from a fitted [catmech_audit_plan()].

Usage

catmech_audit_power(
  plan = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  target_ratio = 1.25,
  power_target = 0.8,
  error_rate = 0.15,
  correlation = 0.85,
  r_squared = 0.3,
  fractions = seq(0.02, 0.4, by = 0.02),
  n_sim = 2000L,
  seed = 42L
)

Arguments

plan

Optional fitted `catmech_audit_plan` object. If supplied, the empirical distribution of \(k\) is used to evaluate power.

N

Total cohort size (number of patient records). Required if `plan` is `NULL`.

target_ratio

Maximum acceptable confidence interval width relative to an ideal full audit (default 1.25, meaning within 25% of the full-audit width).

power_target

Desired statistical power (default 0.80).

error_rate

Anticipated error or corruption rate \(p \in (0, 1)\) (default 0.15). Ignored if `plan` is supplied.

correlation

Anticipated correlation between recorded and true values (default 0.85). Ignored if `plan` is supplied.

r_squared

Anticipated auxiliary predictor \(R^2\) (default 0.30). Ignored if `plan` is supplied.

fractions

Numeric vector of audit fractions to evaluate, strictly between 0 and 1. Defaults to `seq(0.02, 0.40, by = 0.02)`.

n_sim

Number of Monte Carlo draws for evaluating the sampling distribution of the precision ratio (default 2000).

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducible power evaluation.

Value

An object of class `catmech_audit_power` containing:

table

Data frame of evaluated audit fractions, audit sample sizes, expected relative widths, and statistical power.

recommended

Recommended minimum audit fraction and sample size reaching `power_target`.

target_ratio

The target precision ratio evaluated.

power_target

The target statistical power.

N

Total cohort size.

k_summary

Point estimate and uncertainty bounds for the two-phase variance factor \(k\).

Examples

pwr <- catmech_audit_power(N = 500, target_ratio = 1.3, n_sim = 200, seed = 1)
print(pwr)
